payload.name: Verify existing memory before SKIP decision
payload.description: When a construction candidate would be skipped as already represented, verify that a matching memory actually exists in the retrieved existing-memory pool before selecting SKIP; if no matching memory is found, choose ADD.
content: Before applying SKIP to a candidate with the reason 'already represented', explicitly search the retrieved existing-memory pool for a memory that covers the same subject, predicate, and key details.
If no such memory is found in the retrieved pool, do not SKIP the candidate; create it with ADD (or MERGE/UPDATE only if a partially related memory exists).
SKIP is only valid when the exact fact is demonstrably present in the visible memory pool; absence of the fact is not a reason to discard the candidate.

solves: Construction decisions sometimes skip adding a candidate because they assume the fact already exists in memory, even when the retrieved existing-memory pool contains no matching memory. This causes durable facts to be lost. The fix is a reusable rule: before choosing SKIP on the grounds that a candidate is already represented, the agent must confirm the matching memory is actually present in the retrieved pool; if it is absent, ADD the candidate. This applies to any future construction batch where a candidate seems redundant but the pool does not contain the corresponding memory.
